study: Independent-Seed Replication of SAC Regularization Effects
research_questions: Does stronger residual-action regularization consistently reduce regressions across new SAC training seeds?
Does the reduction in regressions come at the cost of fewer rescues?
Does the effect remain after validation-based checkpoint selection?
Are the previously observed ES/WS regional effects reproducible?

hypotheses.H1: Arm B tends to have fewer paired regressions than Arm A.
hypotheses.H2: Arm B can also reduce rescues.
hypotheses.H3: After validation checkpoint selection, the success-rate difference between arms may be smaller.
hypotheses.H4_ES: In ES, Arm B may have more regressions than Arm A.
hypotheses.H4_WS: In WS, Arm B may have fewer regressions than Arm A.

training.execution: 20 runs executed serially; separate run directories; resumable only from complete model/replay/RNG/environment snapshots; completed or mismatched runs are never overwritten

per_seed: Arm A and Arm B success rate
Arm A and Arm B rescue count (BC failure to SAC success)
Arm A and Arm B regression count (BC success to SAC failure)
Regression Count Difference = Arm B minus Arm A
Rescue Count Difference = Arm B minus Arm A
Success Rate Difference in percentage points

secondary.comparison: Arm A Validation-selected vs Arm B Validation-selected
metrics: difference from BC in percentage points

per_seed_metrics: regression rate conditional on BC success
rescue rate conditional on BC failure

training_diagnostics: mean and maximum residual action norm
action saturation frequency (any normalized residual component absolute value >= 0.95)
effective residual correction after action clipping
outcomes.direct_td_error_and_q1_q2_disagreement: Not Available unless directly logged; critic loss is not a substitute

rule_order: highest success rate on the 500 Validation episodes
fewest paired regressions vs BC Only on the same positions
checkpoint_selection.before_final: record all 60 model checkpoint SHA-256 values, all Validation result SHA-256 values, selections, BC checkpoint SHA-256, and evaluation ranges in a frozen JSON manifest

bootstrap.method: paired training-seed percentile bootstrap with replacement

statistical_analysis.exact_sign_test: two-sided binomial sign test on non-tied training-seed effects

position_level.test: exact McNemar on paired initial positions
position_level.families: Holm correction across the 10 seeds within each endpoint and checkpoint comparison; fixed-30k primary and selected-checkpoint secondary are separate families

regional_tests.fixed_30k: paired exact McNemar for ES/WS regression conditional on BC success and rescue conditional on BC failure, by seed; one Holm family across the 40 tests (2 regions × 2 endpoints × 10 seeds)
regional_tests.selected_checkpoints: same tests reported as secondary with a separate Holm family across 40 tests
regional_tests.regional_effect_uncertainty: report seed-level paired rate differences and bootstrap confidence intervals across training seeds

statistical_analysis.dependence_caveat: Positions are shared across models and training seeds. Position-level tests condition on these fixed positions and policies; 20000 episodes are not 20000 independent training samples. Do not infer training-seed population effects from position-level p-values.

decision_criteria.interpretation: Exploratory progression criteria only; not substitutes for statistical evidence or proof of universal improvement/safety
